LESSON: INTERACTIVE SPEAKING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.8: Interactive Speaking

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Interactive Speaking. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you actively participate in a conversation?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify vocabulary related to the theme for comprehension
2. apply appropriate turn-taking in oral communication
3. appreciate the role of speaking clearly for effective communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: INTERACTIVE SPEAKING
Subject: MANDARIN · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Interactive Speaking helps you succeed in MANDARIN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: INTERACTIVE SPEAKING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify vocabulary related to the theme for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to identify vocabulary related to the theme for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify vocabulary related to the theme for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Interactive Speaking”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify vocabulary related to the theme for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply appropriate turn-taking in oral communication

What this means
In this part you learn to apply appropriate turn-taking in oral communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply appropriate turn-taking in oral communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Interactive Speaking to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply appropriate turn-taking in oral communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of speaking clearly for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of speaking clearly for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of speaking clearly for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of speaking clearly for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Interactive Speaking is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Interactive Speaking”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify vocabulary related to the theme for comprehension)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Interactive Speaking to a partner. (skill: apply appropriate turn-taking in oral communication)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of speaking clearly for effective communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Interactive Speaking to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify vocabulary related to the theme for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: apply appropriate turn-taking in oral communication.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of speaking clearly for effective communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Interactive Speaking from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Interactive Speaking: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Interactive Speaking?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you actively participate in a conversation?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Interactive Speaking means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify vocabulary related to the theme for comprehension.
5. Be able to: apply appropriate turn-taking in oral communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
